Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
   
 
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
Pacific Gas and Electric Company 
 
 
Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
PREPARED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF 
JENS NEDRUD 
TCLL INTERCONNECTION STUDY PROCESSES 
ON BEHALF OF 
PACIFIC GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY 
NOVEMBER 16, 2026

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 1 of 37 
 
PACIFIC GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY 
1 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
2 
TCLL INTERCONNECTION STUDY PROCESSES 
3 
I. 
Introduction 
4 
Q.   
Please state your name, title, and business address. 
5 
A.   
My name is Jens Nedrud and I am Director, Electric Transmission Planning 
6 
with Pacific Gas and Electric Company (“PG&E”).  My business address is 
7 
300 Lakeside Drive, Oakland, California. 
8 
Q.   
Please briefly describe your current responsibilities at PG&E. 
9 
A.   
I oversee the interconnection of wholesale and retail load to PG&E’s electric 
10 
transmission grid.  I also oversee the transmission planning for PG&E’s 
11 
transmission grid enhancements to meet future growth on the system to support 
12 
the California Independent System Operator Corporation (“CAISO”) 
13 
Transmission Planning Process (“TPP”) and comply with federal planning 
14 
criteria. 
15 
Q.   
Please summarize your educational and professional background. 
16 
A.   
I earned a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from the University of 
17 
Washington in 2004 and a Master of Science in Electrical Engineering from 
18 
the same university in 2006.  I am a licensed professional engineer in 
19 
Washington with 20 years of utility experience, leading engineering functions 
20 
such as substation design, distribution and transmission planning, and asset 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 2 of 37 
 
health planning.  I have extensive experience planning transmission system 
1 
projects across the Northwest and California. 
2 
Q.   
What is the purpose of your testimony? 
3 
A.   
The purpose of my testimony is to describe PG&E’s current process for 
4 
studying Wholesale Load Interconnections and to identify and explain the new 
5 
study processes PG&E is proposing to adopt to accommodate requests for 
6 
wholesale interconnection service by entities that PG&E’s Transmission 
7 
Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”) identifies as “Transmission Customers for Large 
8 
Load” or “TCLLs.”  In particular, I will explain how the proposed changes to 
9 
the TO Tariff address the concerns reflected in the Order to Show Cause 
10 
(“OSC”) issued by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or 
11 
“Commission”) regarding study procedures for TCLLs.   
12 
II. 
Concerns Expressed in the OSC Regarding Study Processes  
13 
Q. 
Can you summarize your understanding of the Commission’s concerns that 
14 
are relevant to your testimony and area of expertise?  
15 
A. 
The Commission generally expressed concern that the CAISO and TO Tariffs 
16 
lack provisions that address “with sufficient clarity and consistency” how the 
17 
CAISO and/or the Participating Transmission Owners (“Participating TO”) 
18 
will timely study the provision of transmission service to Eligible Customers 
19 
on behalf of Large Loads.  The Commission observed that the CAISO does not 
20 
appear to conduct studies to determine the necessary network upgrades needed 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 3 of 37 
 
for the provision of transmission service outside of its TPP.1  FERC thus 
1 
directed the CAISO and 
 to explain whether their tariffs 
2 
remain just and reasonable without, among other things, study procedures that 
3 
address the unique characteristics and challenges of providing transmission 
4 
service or to amend their tariffs to do so.2 
5 
Q. 
How do the CAISO and the Participating TOs study the provision of 
6 
transmission service to Eligible Customers as contemplated under the OSC?   
7 
A. 
Mr. Virani’s testimony provides a more fulsome explanation, but I also will 
8 
touch on this issue.  The CAISO does not have a specific process for entities to 
9 
apply for transmission service like other regions.  Similarly, the CAISO region 
10 
does not have a process for studying specific requests for transmission service 
11 
like the traditional process contemplated by the Commission’s pro forma Open 
12 
Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT”).  Rather, the CAISO engages in 
13 
transmission planning holistically for the entire Balancing Authority Area 
14 
(“BAA”) and the Participating TOs engage in their own planning in 
15 
coordination with the CAISO to ensure delivery is possible over their 
16 
transmission facilities.  My understanding is that the CAISO is not intending to 
17 
change this process.   
18 
The Commission indicated in the OSC that to the extent the CAISO or 
19 
 
1  OSC at P 39. 
2  Id. at P 40.

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 4 of 37 
 
the Participating TOs already have procedures and conduct “such studies,” 
1 
(i.e., transmission service request studies) but those processes are not included 
2 
in their tariffs, that the CAISO and Participating TOs could amend their tariffs 
3 
so that the study process was clearer.3  To address this concern, PG&E 
4 
proposes to create a new interconnection process to study TCLL 
5 
Interconnections.  Specifically, in paragraph 25 of the OSC, FERC mentions 
6 
that the TO Tariff (Wholesale Load) interconnection process “does not grant 
7 
transmission service; rather, the applicant must retain the services of a 
8 
Scheduling Coordinator to access transmission service over the CAISO-
9 
controlled grid.”  The Commission is correct that the existing Wholesale Load 
10 
interconnection process (retitled “Wholesale Load Interconnection” process) 
11 
does not “grant transmission service.”  However, it serves a similar purpose 
12 
because once the facilities found to be required for Wholesale Load 
13 
Interconnection service are planned in coordination with the CAISO and then 
14 
constructed, Wholesale Customers’ Scheduling Coordinators need not request 
15 
or be studied further to schedule power on a firm basis.   
16 
Q. 
Does the TO Tariff address Wholesale Load Interconnections to a particular 
17 
Participating TO? 
18 
A. 
Yes, all the Participating TOs’ existing Wholesale Load Interconnection 
19 
processes are limited to Wholesale Customers in light of FERC’s jurisdiction.  
20 
 
3  OSC at P 62.

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 5 of 37 
 
The “retail service” request process, just like the Wholesale Load 
1 
Interconnection process, results in the studies being performed that, when 
2 
coupled with the TPP, mean that the Scheduling Coordinators for retail load 
3 
likewise need not request or be studied further to schedule power on a firm 
4 
basis.  In short, the Participating TOs and the CAISO share responsibility for 
5 
conducting studies that ensure that all Load ultimately is served.  Today, a 
6 
Large Load End User in PG&E’s service area would request retail service and 
7 
a PG&E study process would commence.  If the Large Load End User were 
8 
not in PG&E’s service area, Participating TO studies would occur under the 
9 
respective Participating TO’s TO Tariff.  In both cases, the CAISO TPP would 
10 
ultimately determine what facilities need to be constructed to ensure that a 
11 
Scheduling Coordinator could schedule firm power to the Large Load End 
12 
User.   
13 
Q. 
How are you proposing to change the existing processes to satisfy the OSC? 
14 
A. 
The changes being proposed are based on the existing roles and 
15 
responsibilities.  As my colleague Mr. Virani explains, it is the TO Tariff 
16 
interconnection process, coupled with the CAISO’s TPP, that will continue to 
17 
be the means of ensuring that Scheduling Coordinators can schedule to 
18 
particular Loads, including Large Load End Users.  However, a new process is 
19 
being created to study Large Load End Users whose TCLL interconnects to, or 
20 
seeks to interconnect to, PG&E’s transmission system.  Under this process, all 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 6 of 37 
 
Large Load End Users whose TCLLs connect or seek to connect to PG&E’s 
1 
facilities, including those who seek service from PG&E as a TCLL, will be 
2 
studied under a single tariff, regardless of their retail transmission provider.  
3 
And, that process will interact with the CAISO TPP much in the same manner 
4 
as the other existing retail and wholesale study processes.   
5 
Q. 
Can you provide more detail as to what concerns were identified by the OSC 
6 
as relates to the performance of studies for Large Load End Users? 
7 
A. 
The specific concerns about studies include 
study process that 
8 
considered the unique characteristics and impacts of large loads, such as 
9 
studies that evaluate the transmission system’s ability to withstand risks 
10 
observed from analyzed large load behavior.4  FERC noted that accurate 
11 
models using electromagnetic transient studies might help to ensure that 
12 
transmission service needed on behalf of large loads can be provided without 
13 
compromising reliability.5  It also noted the absence of clear and consistent 
14 
provisions requiring the evaluation of alternative transmission technologies 
15 
that can meet transmission needs more efficiently or cost-effectively than 
16 
traditional network upgrades.6  The Commission noted that, “based on the 
17 
record, it appears reasonable that such study processes, culminating in a report 
18 
to the [TCLL] with the results of the studies, including any Direct Assignment 
19 
 
4  OSC at P 48. 
5  OSC at P 59. 
6  Id. at P 60.

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 7 of 37 
 
Facilities and network upgrades necessary to accommodate the transmission 
1 
service request as well as a non-binding good-faith estimate of the cost and the 
2 
time to construct such facilities, should take no more than 60-90 calendar days 
3 
to complete.”7 
4 
As I describe below, PG&E proposes to address those concerns through 
5 
a new TCLL Interconnection process.  However, before discussing that 
6 
process, I think it would be helpful to provide some background on how PG&E 
7 
currently studies Wholesale Load Interconnections under its TO Tariff.  
8 
III. 
PG&E’s Existing Wholesale Load Interconnection study process 
9 
Q. 
What is the purpose of PG&E’s existing Wholesale Load study process? 
10 
A.   
When a new Wholesale Load customer seeks to interconnect to PG&E’s 
11 
transmission system or an existing Wholesale Load customer seeks to modify 
12 
or expand an existing Wholesale Load Interconnection, PG&E must study the 
13 
request to determine the impacts on its transmission system.  Specifically, a 
14 
study is necessary to identify whether there is adequate transmission capacity 
15 
to safely and reliably interconnect new or incremental Wholesale Load to 
16 
PG&E’s electrical system.  The process analyzes the impacts of 
17 
interconnecting the Load and identifies any upgrades that will be required to 
18 
accommodate the Load on the transmission system.  
19 
 
7  Id. at P 62.

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 8 of 37 
 
Q. 
Under PG&E’s existing process, how does the Company process applications 
1 
seeking to interconnect Wholesale Load? 
2 
A. 
Mr. Virani’s testimony describes the application process and the nature of the 
3 
customers seeking what is now called a “Wholesale Load Interconnection.”  
4 
After determining that an application is complete, in a typical situation, the 
5 
Company tenders a System Impact Study Agreement within 20 Business Days 
6 
of receipt of a Completed Wholesale Load Interconnection Application.  The 
7 
System Impact Study Agreement defines, among other things, the scope, 
8 
content, and assumptions of the study to be completed by the Participating TO, 
9 
and the estimated time required to complete it.  At the time of execution, the 
10 
applicant is also required to pay the reasonable estimated cost of performing 
11 
the study.  Sections 10.3 and 10.4 set out the timelines for each of these steps.  
12 
If a System Impact Study indicates that additions or upgrades to the ISO 
13 
Controlled Grid are needed to satisfy an applicant’s request for 
14 
Interconnection, the final step is a Facilities Study under Sections 10.7 and 
15 
10.8. 
16 
Q.   
Please describe the existing Wholesale Load study process. 
17 
A.   
PG&E’s existing TO Tariff outlines the study process for Wholesale Load in 
18 
Sections 10.4 through 10.8.  As I explained above, PG&E uses two separate 
19 
studies to analyze Wholesale Loads:  a System Impact Study and, if needed, a 
20 
Facilities Study.  First, as outlined in Section 10.6 of the TO Tariff, in a typical 
21 
situation, PG&E completes a System Impact Study.  The System Impact Study 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 9 of 37 
 
identifies and analyzes any transmission additions or upgrades that are 
1 
necessary to interconnect and serve the Wholesale Load.  The System Impact 
2 
Study will also identify any adverse impact on Encumbrances.   
3 
Q.   
How long does the Company have to complete the System Impact Study? 
4 
A.   
Section 10.6 indicates the Company will use “due diligence” to complete the 
5 
System Impact Study within 60 calendar days.  In PG&E’s experience, 
6 
generally, the System Impact Study process takes the full 60 days to complete 
7 
and can require more time, especially when multiple applications are in the 
8 
study process. 
9 
Q. 
What happens after the System Impact Study?  
10 
A.   
If the System Impact Study shows that the request can be accommodated 
11 
without Direct Assignment Facilities, Reliability Upgrades, or implementing 
12 
operating procedures, the applicant must request and execute a Wholesale 
13 
Load Interconnection Agreement that will allow them to interconnect to the 
14 
PG&E transmission system or modify their existing Wholesale Load 
15 
Interconnection Agreement.  If the study shows that such facilities or upgrades 
16 
are likely needed, the next step is generally a Facilities Study, as provided in 
17 
Sections 10.7 and 10.8.  
18 
The Facilities Study is a more refined analysis of the impact of interconnecting 
19 
the Wholesale Load to the PG&E transmission system as compared to the 
20 
System Impact Study.  The results of the Facilities Study will refine the cost of 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 10 of 37 
 
the equipment, engineering, procurement and construction work (including 
1 
overheads) needed to interconnect to the PG&E system.  This gives the 
2 
applicant a firmer understanding of its cost responsibility before it signs a 
3 
Wholesale Load Interconnection Agreement.   
4 
Q. 
Does Section 10 offer any alternative to that sequence? 
5 
A. 
Yes.  Some applicants would rather move forward quickly than wait for a 
6 
Facilities Study to refine the cost estimate.  Section 10.12 allows an applicant, 
7 
after it receives the System Impact Study for the proposed Wholesale Load 
8 
Interconnection, to request an Expedited Wholesale Load Interconnection 
9 
Agreement.  Under the expedited process, the applicant proceeds based on 
10 
PG&E’s best estimate of costs of any needed Direct Assignment Facilities and, 
11 
if applicable, Reliability Upgrades, rather than a refined estimate, and agrees to 
12 
pay the actual costs PG&E reasonably incurs. 
13 
Q. 
What types of facilities are identified in these studies? 
14 
A. 
The upgrades are grouped into three categories, Direct Assignment Facilities, 
15 
Reliability Upgrades, and transmission network upgrades.   
16 
Q. 
How does PG&E’s study process interact with CAISO’s study and planning 
17 
process? 
18 
A. 
As already discussed, Participating TOs such as PG&E are responsible for 
19 
studying Wholesale Load Interconnections, and the CAISO is responsible for 
20 
transmission planning generally through the TPP as well as Generation 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 11 of 37 
 
Interconnections to the CAISO Controlled Grid.  The results of PG&E’s 
1 
Wholesale Load studies (wholesale and retail) impact the CAISO planning 
2 
process in two distinct ways.  First, when PG&E submits the Wholesale Load 
3 
Interconnection study results to the CAISO for review in their load 
4 
concurrence process, both the Reliability Upgrades and the transmission 
5 
network upgrades are submitted to the CAISO for their review and 
6 
concurrence for inclusion in the TPP.  In addition, the Load identified in 
7 
Wholesale Load Interconnection studies, along with other retail load growth is 
8 
considered in the TPP process and can trigger upgrades.  As a result of these 
9 
two steps, both the upgrades needed to interconnect Wholesale Loads and the 
10 
Load itself are integrated into the CAISO’s transmission planning process.  
11 
Q. 
Can a Wholesale Load customer interconnect to PG&E’s electrical system if 
12 
there is not sufficient transmission capability to accommodate its full load? 
13 
A.   
Yes.  As part of the study process, to the extent that upgrades are required to 
14 
serve the full Load, PG&E will identify the portion of the requested Load that 
15 
can be accommodated without any Direct Assignment Facilities or Reliability 
16 
Upgrades.  To the extent the applicant is interested, Section 10.11 allows them 
17 
to elect partial interim service up to the level of identified partial interim 
18 
service capability until the required facilities or upgrades are placed in service. 
19

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 12 of 37 
 
IV. 
The TCLL Interconnection Study Processes  
1 
Q.   
How is PG&E proposing to change its TO Tariff to address the requirements 
2 
of the OSC for studying Large Loads?   
3 
A.   
PG&E is proposing to add a new section (Section 10A) to its TO Tariff to 
4 
address TCLL Interconnections.  PG&E proposes using a Serial Study Process 
5 
for TCLL requests that do not impact other customers on the transmission 
6 
system.  In addition, PG&E proposes using a new Cluster Study Process for 
7 
TCLL requests that impact other customers.  I will discuss both processes in 
8 
turn. 
9 
Q.   
What is the first step after a TCLL Interconnection Application is deemed 
10 
complete? 
11 
A. 
Within 15 Business Days of PG&E deeming an application complete, the 
12 
Company will perform an Electrical Independence Test to determine if the 
13 
Large Load End User associated with the TCLL’s Interconnection request 
14 
qualifies as an Electrically Independent Large Load.  The one exception is a 
15 
request associated with a Co-Located Large Load End User, which is always 
16 
studied in the Cluster Study Process, as I discuss later in my testimony. 
17

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 13 of 37 
 
Q. 
What is an Electrically Independent Large Load? 
1 
A. 
As indicated in the proposed TO Tariff definition, an Electrically Independent 
2 
Large Load is one where its interconnection impacts are not materially affected 
3 
by one or more other projects.  In these instances, the interconnecting Large 
4 
Load End User and corresponding upgrade facilities would not impact other 
5 
Load interconnections.  For example, additional Load in an unconstrained 
6 
portion of the PG&E system (e.g., which does not depend on pre-identified 
7 
transmission upgrades to meet the aggregate Load), and where the incremental 
8 
Load does not affect other planned projects or would not be expected to impact 
9 
other interconnections would be considered electrically independent.  As a 
10 
result, PG&E can study this Large Load End User without needing to assume 
11 
the status, timing, or configuration of other queued projects.  
12 
Q. 
How do you determine if the Large Load End User is electrically 
13 
independent? 
14 
A. 
To determine whether a Large Load End User is electrically independent, 
15 
PG&E will conduct an Electrical Independence Test under proposed Section 
16 
10A.3.1.  This test requires PG&E to perform the incremental power flow and 
17 
aggregate power flow tests, which look at whether the request, on its own and 
18 
together with other requests, would cause issues on the CAISO Controlled 
19 
Grid.  If the TCLL Interconnection request does not pass the CAISO 
20 
Controlled Grid incremental power flow and aggregate power flow tests, then 
21 
it fails the evaluation of electrical independence for the CAISO Controlled 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 14 of 37 
 
Grid, and the request must be studied with the other electrically dependent 
1 
requests in the Cluster Study Process under proposed Section 10A.5 or 
2 
withdraw.  If it passes, the Large Load End User qualifies as an Electrically 
3 
Independent Load, and the request proceeds under the Serial Study Process 
4 
pursuant to proposed Section 10A.4. 
5 
Q. 
Why does that matter? 
6 
A. 
Because an Electrically Independent Large Load interconnection does not 
7 
impact other interconnection applications, it can be studied independent of 
8 
other interconnection requests and therefore can be completed using the Serial 
9 
Study Process which can be completed in the timeframe the Commission 
10 
envisions in the OSC, if the TCLL opts out of a Facilities Study.  A TCLL that 
11 
requests Interim Standard Interconnection Service and/or Flexible Interim 
12 
Large Load Interconnection Service, however, will need a Facilities Study, 
13 
because that is where PG&E identifies and estimates the cost of the TCLL 
14 
FILLI Facilities. Note that consistent with the TO Tariff, I refer to Flexible 
15 
Interim Large Load Interconnection Service as FILLI Interconnection Service.  
16 
And when discussing both Interim Standard Interconnection Service and FILLI 
17 
Interconnection Service together, I refer to it as Interim Service. 
18 
Q. 
What happens after the Electrical Independence Test? 
19 
A. 
PG&E will hold a scoping meeting with the TCLL within 5 Business Days of 
20 
completing the Electrical Independence Test.  The purpose of the meeting is to 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 15 of 37 
 
address the preliminary interconnection scope, discuss the Point of 
1 
Withdrawal, present preliminary planning assumptions, and assess available 
2 
system capacity.   Within 15 Business Days after the meeting, the TCLL must 
3 
elect to proceed under the applicable Serial Study Process or withdraw its 
4 
TCLL Interconnection Application.  If it withdraws at this point, it receives 
5 
back the unspent portion of its study deposit.  If the Large Load End User is 
6 
electrically dependent, it will proceed under the Cluster Study Process in 
7 
proposed section 10A.5. 
8 
V. 
Serial Study Process 
9 
Q. 
Describe the Serial Study Process that applies to Electrically Independent 
10 
Large Loads. 
11 
A. 
If a System Impact Study Agreement is required, the Participating TO will 
12 
present it to the TCLL at the scoping meeting.  The TCLL then is expected to 
13 
notify the Participating TO within 15 Business Days whether it elects to 
14 
proceed with preparation of a System Impact Study Agreement or withdraw its 
15 
TCLL Interconnection Application.  The TCLL then must execute the System 
16 
Impact Study Agreement and return it to the Participating TO within 15 
17 
Business Days upon receipt.  If the TCLL does not sign, its application is 
18 
deemed withdrawn and any unused deposit and security are returned after 
19 
PG&E’s reasonably incurred costs are covered.  If the TCLL disputes the 
20 
agreement and asks that it be filed unexecuted, the study is put on hold until 
21 
FERC acts.  Upon receipt of an executed System Impact Study Agreement, the 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 16 of 37 
 
Participating TO will use due diligence to complete the required System 
1 
Impact Study within a 60 Business Day period.  The System Impact Study will 
2 
identify whether any Direct Assignment Facilities and TCLL Interconnection 
3 
Network Upgrades are required and provide an estimated cost for such 
4 
facilities.  These terms are all defined in the TO Tariff, and I will discuss them 
5 
further below.  The System Impact Study will also identify any adverse impact 
6 
on Encumbrances existing as of the TCLL’s Completed Application Date.  The 
7 
Participating TO will consider alternative transmission technologies in the 
8 
System Impact Study process.  If traditional network upgrades are selected 
9 
instead of alternative transmission technologies, the Participating TO will 
10 
provide a demonstration of why alternative transmission technologies are not 
11 
feasible or would not result in lower costs or a faster timeline for 
12 
accommodating the TCLL Interconnection.  
13 
Q. 
What happens after the System Impact Study is complete? 
14 
A. 
Within 15 Business Days of completion of the System Impact Study, the TCLL 
15 
decides how it wants to proceed.  If it is satisfied with the results, it may 
16 
request that the Participating TO tender a TCLL Agreement, Facilities 
17 
Agreement, and Cost Assurance Agreement in accordance with Section 
18 
10A.4.8.  If it wants a more refined cost estimate, or if it is seeking Interim 
19 
Standard Interconnection Service and/or FILLI Interconnection Service, it 
20 
must request that the Participating TO tender a Facilities Study Agreement 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 17 of 37 
 
pursuant to Section 10A.4.5.  Alternatively, the TCLL may withdraw its 
1 
application.  If a TCLL requests a Facilities Study Agreement, the Participating 
2 
TO will provide a Facilities Study Agreement within 15 Business Days that 
3 
defines the scope, content, assumptions and terms of reference for such study; 
4 
the estimated time required to complete the required study; and such other 
5 
provisions as the parties may reasonably require.  The TCLL shall execute the 
6 
Facilities Study Agreement and return it to the Participating TO within 15 
7 
Business Days.  Upon receipt of an executed Facilities Study Agreement, the 
8 
Participating TO will use due diligence to complete the required Facilities 
9 
Study within a 60-Business Day period.  The Facilities Study refines the cost 
10 
estimates from the System Impact Study and identifies any TCLL FILLI 
11 
Facilities, if applicable.   
12 
Q. 
What happens after the Facilities Study is complete? 
13 
A. 
Within 15 Business Days of receipt of the completed Facilities Study, the 
14 
TCLL shall request the Participating TO to tender a TCLL Agreement, 
15 
Facilities Agreement, Cost Assurance Agreement, and the optional Interim 
16 
Service Agreement in accordance with Section 10A.4.8 or withdraw its 
17 
application.   
18 
Q. 
What happens once PG&E tenders those agreements? 
19 
A. 
The parties then negotiate and execute the TCLL Agreement, Facilities 
20 
Agreement, Cost Assurance Agreement, and, if applicable, the Interim Service 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 18 of 37 
 
Agreement.  The TO Tariff gives the parties 60 Business Days, which can be 
1 
extended if negotiations are progressing, to negotiate and execute the 
2 
agreements and ensure the relevant agreements, if any, are executed by the 
3 
Large Load End User.  If the parties cannot reach agreement, the TCLL can 
4 
ask that the agreements be filed unexecuted so that FERC can resolve the 
5 
dispute.  If the TCLL withdraws its application, the TCLL shall reimburse the 
6 
Participating TO for the costs reasonably incurred in processing the 
7 
application, after which its remaining security will be released. 
8 
Q. 
Can you explain how the Direct Assignment Facilities, TCLL 
9 
Interconnection Network Upgrades, and/or TCLL FILLI Facilities are 
10 
identified? 
11 
A. 
Generally, the study process identifies all facilities and equipment needed to 
12 
safely and reliably interconnect the proposed Large Load End User.  Of that 
13 
equipment, the Direct Assignment Facilities are those that are owned by the 
14 
Participating TO that are necessary to physically and electrically interconnect 
15 
the TCLL to the ISO Controlled Grid at the point of interconnection.  Although 
16 
this equipment will be at a transmission voltage, it is not part of the ISO 
17 
controlled transmission system.  In contrast, TCLL Interconnection Network 
18 
Upgrades are the additional facilities needed to expand the transmission system 
19 
from the ISO Controlled Grid to the point of interconnection of the TCLL.  
20 
TCLL FILLI Facilities are analogous to the Direct Assignment Facilities in 
21 
that they are used exclusively by a Large Load End User taking FILLI 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 19 of 37 
 
Interconnection Service and are required to provide the flexible non-firm 
1 
interim service until the Participating TO and TCLL have completed 
2 
installation and commissioning of all equipment necessary for Standard 
3 
Interconnection Service.  
4 
A. 
Cluster Study Process 
5 
Q. 
Why does the Serial Study Process not work for all TCLL Interconnections? 
6 
A. 
It has been my experience that a request to interconnect a significant amount of 
7 
load, such as a request associated with a Large Load End User, can have 
8 
electrical impacts on other customers.  The ability of PG&E to interconnect a 
9 
Large Load may be dependent on other requests from Large Load End Users

on PG&E’s transmission system that are being analyzed at the same time.  As a 
11 
result, if PG&E were to study such Electrically Dependent Large Loads 
12 
sequentially, the Company would have to complete each study, and the 
13 
applicant would need to decide on whether to proceed, before finalizing the 
14 
evaluation of additional interconnection requests.  This would be time 
15 
consuming and could result in a number of restudies as applicants drop out of 
16 
the interconnection queue or change their Load configurations based on study 
17 
results.  PG&E already studies all retail service requests for large customers 
18 
(those > 20 MW) using a cluster study process because it is more cost effective 
19 
and efficient for the customers.  PG&E proposes to use this cluster study 
20 
process as the basis for the proposed Cluster Study for TCLLs (who will now

seek interconnection service on behalf of Large Load End Users).  PG&E will 
1 
continue to use the retail cluster study process for those larger customers (e.g., 
2 
20 MW to 49.99 MW loads) that are not Large Load End Users.   
3

When does the Cluster Study Process begin, and which applications are 
4 
included? 
5 
A. 
PG&E will run one Cluster Study each year.  Each year has a closing date of 
6 
the last day of February, by which an application must be complete and found

to be Electrically Dependent, or involve a Co-Located Large Load End User, to 
8 
be included in that year’s cluster.  The Cluster Study Process will begin on the 
9 
first day of April, or the next Business Day, each year.  A fixed annual 
10 
schedule allows us to study all of the Electrically Dependent Large Load 
11 
requests together using the same assumptions and gives TCLLs and their Large 
12 
Load End Users certainty about when their requests will be studied.  Because 
13 
the new process will only just be taking effect, the TO Tariff also recognizes 
14 
that if no Completed TCLL Interconnection Applications have been found to 
15 
be electrically dependent by the last day of February in 2027, there will be no 
16 
Cluster Study Process beginning on April 1, 2027.  Shortly after the closing 
17 
date, each TCLL signs a Cluster Study Process Agreement.  Where it makes 
18 
sense, PG&E may also divide the Cluster into smaller study groups of requests 
19 
that electrically affect one another, so that each request is studied together with 
20 
the requests that actually matter to it.

How does the Company propose to conduct the Cluster Study? 
1 
A. 
The Cluster Study Process has two distinct phases.  In Phase 1, PG&E will 
2 
evaluate all projects in the Cluster using studies that include, but are not 
3 
limited to, a short circuit and steady state (thermal and voltage) analysis.  The 
4 
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Study will identify Participating TO’s required facilities to 
5 
mitigate thermal overloads and voltage violations, and address short circuit, 
6 
stability, and other reliability issues associated with the requested service.  The 
7 
Phase 1 Study shall (i) evaluate the impact of all TCLL Interconnection 
8 
requests in the cluster; (ii) preliminarily identify for each TCLL

Interconnection request the required Direct Assignment Facilities, TCLL 
10 
Interconnection Network Upgrades, and TCLL FILLI Facilities; (iii) assess the 
11 
Point of Withdrawal selected by each TCLL and potential alternatives to 
12 
evaluate potential efficiencies in overall system upgrade costs; and (iv) provide 
13 
a good faith estimate of the cost of the Direct Assignment Facilities, TCLL 
14 
Interconnection Network Upgrades, and TCLL FILLI Facilities for each TCLL 
15 
Interconnection request.  We coordinate the Phase 1 Study with the CAISO, 
16 
including the development of Base Cases, so that the impacts on the CAISO 
17 
Controlled Grid are modeled accurately.

A.

in place before Phase 2 begins gives PG&E a clear commitment from the

purposes.  First, it asks TCLLs to demonstrate a meaningful financial

commitment at the point where the study results become more concrete, which

helps ensure that Phase 2 is performed for requests that are likely to move

forward.  Second, PG&E may also use those funds for engineering, design, and

procurement of the Direct Assignment Facilities and TCLL Interconnection

equipment to begin earlier, which can shorten the time to energization.  The

amount it returns at the commercial paper rate, from the date the security was

paid until the date it is refunded.

A.

Phase 1 Study to account for the withdrawal of requests after the Phase 1 Study

process, (ii) identify Direct Assignment Facilities, TCLL Interconnection

Interconnection request a final Point of Withdrawal, and preliminarily identify

any TCLL Reliability Network Upgrades.  Phase 2 also includes a transient 
15

detailed analyses that are most useful once the cluster has been narrowed to the

requests that are moving forward.  When the study identifies system violations,

timeline for accommodating the TCLL Interconnection.

A.

raise concerns with PG&E and the CAISO before they decide whether to

proceed.

Does the Company have experience performing cluster studies for Large 
20 
Loads? 
21 
A. 
Yes, the Company has been performing cluster studies for loads greater than

What has been the Company’s experience to date with these CPUC-
2 
jurisdictional Large Load interconnection requests?

A. 
The Company has found that studying Large Loads collectively as part of a 
4 
cluster has been an effective way to identify needs and plan the solutions

required to interconnect these customers.  In PG&E’s experience, studying

Electrically Dependent Large Load requests on a serial basis is extremely

inefficient.  Each study must be finished, and each applicant must decide

whether to proceed, before the next request can be studied with confidence,

and any change or withdrawal by an earlier request can require later requests to

be restudied.  PG&E has performed 3 Large Load cluster studies thus far,

involving 93 separate applications, with over 25 GW of Load.  If PG&E had 
12 
only used a serial study process, it would have required multiple years to 
13 
evaluate the applications, significantly delaying their interconnection.  By 
14 
using a two-step cluster process, PG&E was able to get phase 1 study results 
15 
back to the applicants in approximately 9 months, giving them actionable 
16 
information to make their business decisions.

Q. 
What is the anticipated timeline for these Cluster Studies? 
18 
A. 
Each phase of the Cluster Study is targeted for completion within 120 Business 
19 
Days and the entire process, including meetings to discuss results, is estimated 
20 
to take over a year.  However, the Company proposes to conduct one Cluster 
21

Study Process annually by allowing for some overlap in each Cluster Study 
1 
Process.

Why do you believe a Cluster Study can be a timelier approach? 
3 
A.   
Studying Electrically Dependent Large Loads together produces more accurate 
4 
results and avoids serial restudies.  In addition, studying a group of interrelated 
5 
projects collectively is more efficient than studying those same projects

sequentially.

under a 90-day time frame will result in numerous restudies and will likely

take far longer to ultimately complete.  For requests that are electrically

independent and do not seek an optional Facilities Study, our proposed TO

Tariff language targets completion of the System Impact Study process within

90 Business Days.

PG&E has been studying “electrically dependent” Large Loads for

several years under a cluster study process and its experience is that such

remains, in my opinion, the most efficient way to conduct studies of the

impacts of Large Load End Users on the transmission system.  The 
22

Commission highlights the reliability impacts of Large Loads on the

transmission system.  This concern is valid and thus, transmission owners, like

reliable interconnection of Large Load End Users.  When such Loads impact

short time period.  Although PG&E understands the urgency of the needs of

technology companies, particularly given its location, those needs cannot be

placed above the safety of the community and PG&E employees.

systems?

the TCLL, and the CAISO, and coordinate any studies needed to assess the

impacts.  PG&E will include the Affected System Operator in meetings with

the TCLL.  Any upgrades needed on the Affected System are the TCLL’s cost

responsibility, because the TCLL’s request is what creates the need for them,

and those costs will be reflected in the Facilities Agreement.  To keep this

coordination from delaying the process, an Affected System Operator that

takes service under PG&E’s TO Tariff must tell us within 40 Business Days

whether it intends to study the TCLL Interconnection Application.  If it does

not respond, it cannot later bring claims against PG&E regarding impacts from

that interconnection.

A.

Interconnection Service, build on the existing partial interim service offered to

traditional Wholesale Loads under Section 10.  A study may show that Interim 
8 
Standard Interconnection Service can be provided to some portion of the total 
9 
amount of Load requested by a TCLL, after certain facilities are built.  As for

the remaining Load, or all the Load if no Interim Standard Interconnection

Service is available, FILLI Interconnection Service is an optional

interconnection service that PG&E and the CAISO are proposing to offer.

PG&E’s study process for FILLI Interconnection Service will investigate the

conditions during which Large Load End Users would need to limit their

Energy withdrawals under certain conditions during the period that network

upgrades are being constructed.  The analysis would also consider what

facilities may be needed and what procedures may need to be adopted to allow

for FILLI Interconnection Service, which is an as-available service.

and FILLI Interconnection Service can be offered, PG&E will study the Load

under NERC Transmission System Planning Performance Requirement

Conditions to determine how much firm service can be offered while upgrades

are being constructed to enable firm service for entire Load request.  This

analysis is performed as part of the otherwise applicable study process, rather

than as a separate process.  As part of that analysis, we will complete a

flexibility needs analysis to quantify when and how FILLI customers may need

to reduce consumption, including the expected magnitude, duration, and

likelihood of those reductions.  That information will allow customers to

understand and plan for potential operating limitations while supporting

reliable interconnection to the transmission system. As part of the FILLI

Interconnection Service evaluation, the Company will evaluate the annual load

ramp of each applicant and identify the expected facilities needed to

accommodate their interim flexible service.

13 
Users 
14 
Q. 
Are there any special conditions associated with studying requests from 
15 
TCLLs when the associated Large Load is co-located with, and at least 
16 
partially supplied by that co-located generation?  
17 
A.   
Yes.  These requests are always studied in the Cluster Study Process.  To the 
18 
extent that a TCLL request indicates that a Co-Located Large Load End User 
19 
commits to using on-site generation to reduce a portion or all of its demand, 
20 
PG&E will study upgrades needed to support the requested level of service.  
21 
That approach only works if we can rely on the Co-Located Large Load End 
22 
User staying at or below the level of service requested in the TCLL 
23

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 31 of 37 
 
Interconnection Application, so our studies will take into account the 
1 
mechanisms the Co-Located Large Load End User proposes to ensure it does 
2 
not withdraw more Energy from the grid than it has requested.  If PG&E and 
3 
the CAISO are not satisfied that those mechanisms are adequate, the Large 
4 
Load must be restudied at the higher level.  In instances where the facility 
5 
wishes to export power onto the transmission system, the Generating Units co-
6 
locating with Large Load End Users are studied under the CAISO Tariff, and 
7 
PG&E and the CAISO will produce study results that reflect the combined 
8 
presence of the Generating Units and Large Loads.  I would expect the CAISO,

as BAA, would be the entity that determines what equipment and protocols are

needed to ensure that no more than a pre-determined amount of generation 
11 
would appear on its system unexpectedly.

Why are requests associated with Co-Located Large Load End Users always 
13 
studied in the Cluster Study Process? 
14 
A. 
A Co-Located Large Load End User raises questions that a standalone load 
15 
does not.  Because the Co-Located Large Load End User is relying on on-site 
16 
generation to serve part of its demand, we have to understand what happens 
17 
when that Generation is unavailable and the Co-Located Large Load End Users 
18 
turns to the grid instead.  That means we need to evaluate the protective 
19 
mechanisms, such as relays, controls, and operating limits, that will keep the 
20 
Co-Located Large Load End User from drawing more from the CAISO 
21 
Controlled Grid than it has requested, and we need to coordinate that 
22

EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 32 of 37 
 
evaluation with the CAISO’s study of the Generating Units co-locating with 
1 
the Large Load End User.  That work takes time, and it cannot reliably be 
2 
completed within the timeframe of the Serial Study Process.  The Cluster 
3 
Study Process, with its two phases and its coordination with the CAISO, gives 
4 
PG&E the time to study those protective mechanisms properly.  It also gives us 
5 
the time to consider, if a Co-Located Large Load End User were to exceed its 
6 
requested capacity, what the consequences should be, including whether

penalties for exceeding that capacity are appropriate, similar to the approach

PJM has taken for co-located load.

Q. 
How will the PG&E study processes interact with the CAISO’s TPP? 
11 
A. 
As discussed earlier, PG&E’s study process can identify transmission upgrades 
12 
that would be triggered by the Large Load End User.  These study results are 
13 
submitted to the CAISO for review in their concurrence process.  In addition,

the load identified in PG&E’s interconnection studies, together with other load

growth, is also considered in the CAISO’s TPP which can also identify if

additional upgrades are required to serve the aggregate load.

Other Issues 
18 
Q. 
FERC mentioned electromagnetic transient studies in the OSC, does PG&E 
19 
include such analysis in its study processes? 
20 
A. 
Yes.  PG&E will perform an electromagnetic transient study for a Large Load 
21 
End User approximately one year before the Load is scheduled to be energized.  
22

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 33 of 37 
 
The timing matters.  An electromagnetic transient study is only as good as the 
1 
models and assumptions that go into it, including the specific equipment, 
2 
inverters, and control settings the Large Load End User will install and the 
3 
condition of the surrounding system when the load comes online.  Early in the 
4 
interconnection process, much of that information is not yet final, so a study 
5 
performed at that stage would rest on assumptions that are likely to change and 
6 
would produce results that are not reliable.  The CAISO faces a similar issue 
7 
on the generation side, where detailed transient analysis is generally performed 
8 
later, once equipment and controls are known.  By performing the study about 
9 
a year ahead of energization, PG&E can use actual equipment data and current 
10 
system conditions, which allows the study to identify issues on the system 
11 
more accurately.  A year also leaves enough time to act on the results, such as 
12 
adjusting control settings or adding protective equipment, before the load is 
13 
energized.  In short, performing the study at that point makes it a realistic and 
14 
actionable study rather than a theoretical one.   
15 
Q. 
How do the various study processes consider the unique characteristics and 
16 
impacts of Large Loads, such as evaluating the transmission system’s ability 
17 
to withstand risks observed from analyzed Large Load behavior? 
18 
A. 
The new NERC Computational Load standards and pending updates to the 
19 
Company’s Transmission Interconnection Handbook will help define a number 
20 
of technical requirements specific to Large Load End Users, including detailed 
21 
operating requirements such as ramp rate limits.  These requirements coupled 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 34 of 37 
 
with detailed stability requirements as proposed in our interconnection study 
1 
process and active monitoring equipment will enable our operators to manage 
2 
these loads to maintain reliability. 
3 
Q. 
Can you explain in more detail how you will examine alternative 
4 
transmission technologies in the study processes? 
5 
A. 
During Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the Large Load Cluster Study Process, once the 
6 
system violations are identified, the transmission planning team will first 
7 
evaluate whether any alternative transmission technology solutions can apply 
8 
to mitigate the violations.  If no alternative transmission technology solution 
9 
applies, transmission planning will proceed with proposals using conventional 
10 
mitigation solutions 
11 
Q. 
The OSC also indicates that study procedures could include readiness 
12 
requirements (i.e., meaningful milestones and/or financial commitments) to 
13 
ensure Large Loads are viable and likely to materialize, does the process 
14 
proposed include such requirements? 
15 
A. 
Mr. Virani addresses the readiness requirements that apply when a TCLL 
16 
submits its application, which is outside the scope of my expertise.  From a 
17 
study perspective, however, the process is structured so that a TCLL must 
18 
affirmatively decide to move forward at each stage, after the scoping meeting, 
19 
after each study, and after each results meeting, or its request is withdrawn.  
20 
That keeps requests that are not progressing from occupying study resources or 
21 
affecting the results for other customers.  In addition, as I noted earlier, a 
22 
TCLL that proceeds to Phase 2 of the Cluster Study must post Phase 2 
23

Docket No. ER27-XXXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0002 
Page 35 of 37 
 
Security, which is a meaningful financial commitment at the point where the 
1 
study results become more concrete.

4 
A.
